chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from a number of his companions, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman al-Sayrafi, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he presented to us food containing roast meat and other items after it. Then he brought a bowl containing rice, so I ate with him. He said, 'Eat.' I said, 'I have already eaten.' He said, 'Eat, for the love of a man for his brother is considered by his extending himself in eating.' Then he marked a portion for me with his finger in the bowl and said to me, 'You must eat up to that,' after I had already eaten. So I ate it.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of extending oneself in eating according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the Shia concept of *mawaddah* (affection) through the physical act of sharing food, insisting that Abdullah ibn Suleiman eat more rice despite being full. The Imam’s gesture of marking the portion with his finger underscores the sincerity of hospitality, where the host’s desire for the guest’s satisfaction transcends mere politeness. This narrative highlights the practical application of brotherhood in daily interactions, emphasizing that true love is manifested in tangible generosity and the sharing of sustenance.
